en: Acyuta, Keśava, Rāma-Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa-Dāmodara, Vāsudeva, Hari.
I worship Śrīdhara, Mādhava, the beloved of the Gopīs, the leader of Jānakī, Rāmacandra. || 1 ||
I bow to Acyuta, Keśava, the husband of Satyabhāmā,
Mādhava, the bearer of Śrī, who is worshipped by Rādhikā.
With his mind, he established the temple of Indirā as beautiful as the Nandana grove, containing the son of Devakī. || 2 ||
To Viṣṇu, the victorious, the bearer of the conch, the wielder of the discus,
the lover of Rukmiṇī, and the husband of Jānakī.
Salutations to You, the beloved of the cowherd girls, the Self who is worshipped, the destroyer of Kaṃsa, and the possessor of the flute. || 3 ||
O Kṛṣṇa, O Govinda, O Rāma, O Nārāyaṇa,
O Lord of Śrī, O Vāsudeva, O Unconquered One, O Treasure of Fortune!
O Acyuta, O Ananta, O Mādhava, O Adhokṣaja, O Leader of Dvārakā, O Protector of Draupadī! || 4 ||
Agitated by the Rākṣasa and graced by Sītā, he was the cause of the sacredness of the Daṇḍaka forest lands.
May Rāghava—accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, served by the monkeys, and honored by Agastya—protect me. || 5 ||
The slayer of Dhenuka and Ariṣṭa, who does not perform the rites of those who hate him, the destroyer of Keśin, the taker of Kaṃsa, and the player of the flute.
May the child Gopāla, who caused the wrath of Pūtanā and who plays with the daughter of the Sun, protect me at all times. || 6 ||
His garment flashed like a flash of lightning,
and his body shone like a cloud in the rainy season.
I worship the lotus-eyed one, whose chest is adorned with a garland of wild flowers and whose pair of feet are crimson.
His face was radiant with curled locks of hair, his head adorned with a jeweled crown, and his cheeks gleaming with earrings.
I worship that dark-complexioned one, resplendent with necklaces, armlets, and bracelets, and charming with tinkling bells. || 8 ||
The person who daily recites with longing and love this "Eightfold Hymn" (Aṣṭaka) to Acyuta, which bestows all desired objects—
By means of conduct, one becomes beautiful; Hari quickly becomes subject to that sustainer of the universe.
Thus ends the Acyutāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
